summary: Suspend external-grant authentication when replicated grants assign opposite profiles to one principal

replay.detail: Existing append-only grant and revocation claims are read without rewriting history. Active opposite-profile grants conflict regardless of replication arrival order; revoked and expired grants do not contribute to the conflict.

schema.detail: Adds the typed client error grant-profile-conflict (GrantProfileConflict in Rust), returned as HTTP 409, plus inspect-only ?witness=1 opt-in conflict and cleared_conflicts witnesses with typed assistant/service profiles and revoked/expired causes. Default grant responses retain their previous shape for old strict clients. No grant claim shape or storage migration changes.

rules.detail: If a principal has active grants in both assistant and service profiles, all of that principal's external grants are suspended, not just the losing or newest profile. Multiple same-profile grants remain allowed. Authentication resumes after replicated append-only revocations or expiry remove the opposite-profile conflict from the local view; service issuance remains disabled. Inspect computes active witnesses and cleared_conflicts witnesses with revoked or expired causes; no conflict state is persisted.

compatibility.detail: Conflict admission counts only well-formed foreign owner grants with authenticated envelope provenance from a keyed, admitted fleet writer, including valid records in degraded envelopes. Policies and revocations count only from the grant's own origin and owner with consistent immutable identity; foreign transitions also require authenticated provenance. Invalid overlays are ignored, retaining the last valid policy. This restriction also applies to local grants. Request-side sealed membership folds populate a separate generation-keyed cache without weakening local sealing. Tokens remain issuer-local. Older members do not enforce suspension, so upgrade all serving members before relying on it.

downtime.detail: No migration downtime is required. Affected people cannot authenticate with any external grant while a profile conflict remains visible; a partition can extend this interruption until revocations replicate. Unaffected people retain existing authentication behavior.

manual.detail: For a conflicted principal, choose the intended profile and append revocations for every active grant in the opposite profile. Let those revocations replicate to each serving issuer; do not delete claims or replace tokens to resolve the conflict.

recovery.detail: After revocations replicate, remaining otherwise-valid grants in the intended profile can authenticate again without reissuance. Expiry of every remaining active opposite-profile grant also clears the conflict; expired and revoked grants remain unusable. If authentication is still suspended on an issuer after revocation, restore replication so it receives the revocations; restarting or changing claim arrival order does not resolve the conflict.
